10. SHOULDER DYSTOCIA (SD)

-incidence 0.58 – 0.70%

- 48% in infants weighing < 4kg

Prediction – 16% by conventional methods

Brachial Plexus Injury:

BPI – is commonest cause of litigation due to SD and 3rd common cause related to obstetrics.

Leads to 10% permanent neurological damage.

Risk factors

Pre labour

1. Previous shoulder dystocia

2. Macrosomia > 4.5kg

3. DM (2 to 4-fold)

4. BMI > 30

5. IOL

Intrapartum:

1. Prolong 1st stage

2. Secondary arrest

3. Prolong 2nd stage

4. Oxytocin augmentation

5. Assisted vaginal delivery.

Diagnosis:

-Difficulty with delivery of face and chin
-Turtle neck sign
-Failure of restitution
-Failure of shoulder to descend
⇨Axial traction can be used

Lateral and any other avoided => nerve avulsion injury

 

Prevention

⇨IOL
-Don’t prevent in non-diabetic macrosomia
-Prevent SD in diabetic macrosomia
⇨Elective C/S consider in DM + EFW > 4.5kg

Post-natal Management of women/ New Born:

Maternal risks:

299.PPH 11%
300.Perineal tear (3rd/4th degree) 38%
301.Vaginal, cervical laceration
302.Bladder rupture
303.Uterine rupture
304.Symphysial separation
305.Sacra iliac joint dislocation
306.Lateral femoral cutaneous neuropathy

Fetal risks:

1. BPI – 2.3 – 16%,

46% of BPI due to substandard care.

10% permanent injury to nerve, 4% during C/S and 12% after simple C/S.

Always document the anterior shoulder as posterior shoulder is never because of health care professionals’ undue traction, post shoulder is always affected by maternal effort

2. Humerus facture.

3. Clavicle fracture.

 

Recurrence:

307.10 times higher = 1 – 25%
308.Either c/s or vaginal birth – joint decision between women and her carer

 

 

Call for help:

Midwife coordinator for documentation, time of SD, arrival of doctor, performance of maneuver, which shoulder is anterior.

Additional midwife help

Neonatologist and

Anesthetist

MC – Robert’s position thighs to abd 90% successful

 

Suprapubic pressure rocking/ continuous

Routine axial traction 90% success

Episiotomy as it will make internal maneuver easier

Risk of humerus

Fracture 2 – 12%
